title: CERT-In Vulnerability Note  CIVN-2026-0526
content:
CERT-In Vulnerability Note 
                                                                      CIVN-2026-0526
Use-After-Free Vulnerability in curl and libcurl
Original Issue Date:October   26, 2026
Severity Rating: HIGH
Software Affected
curl versions 8.12.0 to 8.22.0
libcurl versions corresponding to the affected releases
Overview
A Use-After-Free vulnerability has been reported in curl and libcurl, which could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial-of-service condition on affected systems.
Target Audience:
All organizations and administrators using affected versions of curl and libcurl.
Risk Assessment:
High risk of remote code execution and denial of service under specific conditions.
Impact Assessment:
Successful exploitation could lead to arbitrary code execution or application crashes.
Description
curl is a command-line tool and libcurl is a library used for transferring data over various network protocols, including HTTP and HTTPS.
A Use-After-Free vulnerability exists in curl and libcurl due to improper handling of HTTP/2 stream reset responses received from a server during data uploads.
The vulnerability could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial-of-service condition under specific conditions.
Solution
Apply appropriate security updates and mitigations as recommended by the vendor.
https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-92392.html

curl Project
https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-92392.html

title: CERT-In Vulnerability Note  CIVN-2026-0525
content:
CERT-In Vulnerability Note 
                                                                      CIVN-2026-0525
VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) SQL Injection Vulnerability
Original Issue Date:October   26, 2026
Severity Rating: CRITICAL
Software Affected
VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem 5.2.x prior to 5.2.3.18
VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem 6.1.x prior to 6.1.3.10
VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem 6.4.x prior to 6.4.2.12
Overview
A vulnerability has been reported in VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO), which could allow a remote attacker to escalate privileges and gain unauthorized access to privileged functionality on affected systems.
Target Audience:
Network Administrators, IT Security Professionals, and organizations operating affected on-premises Velo-Cloud Orchestrator (VCO) deployments.
Risk Assessment:
High risk of privilege escalation, data compromise, disruption of network management services.
Impact Assessment:
Potential for unauthorized access to sensitive orchestrator data and information it manages, disruption or compromise of the VCO host.
Description
VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) is a centralized management and orchestration platform used to configure, monitor, and manage VMware VeloCloud SD-WAN networks, including edge devices, network policies, and connectivity across distributed sites.
A vulnerability exist in VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) due to improper neutralization of special elements used in SQL commands. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted request to the targeted VCO web interface using a valid authenticated session.
Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the orchestrator and the data it manages.
Note: This vulnerability (CVE-2026-114625) is being actively exploited in the wild. Users are strongly advised to apply the latest patches immediately.
Solution
Apply appropriate updates as mentioned by the vendor:
https://www.arista.com/en/support/advisories-notices/security-advisory/24838-security-advisory-0199
